audit_notes: The parameter set is internally inconsistent and cannot be fixed within realistic material properties. With first-order hydrolysis and diffusion, the reaction front depth is delta = sqrt(D/k) = sqrt(1e-13/1e-4) = 32 um, and the resulting surface recession is of order v = sqrt(D*k) = sqrt(1e-13*1e-4) = 3.2e-9 m/s = 100 mm per year, about 3000 times faster than the stated erosion rate of 1e-12 m/s (30 um per year); the 0.3 mm film would be gone in about a day. Conversely, reaching 30 um per year with D = 1e-13 m2/s requires k = v^2/D = 1e-11 1/s, and then delta = sqrt(D/k) = 0.1 m, far larger than the film: the whole film would hydrolyse in bulk and lose integrity instead of sloughing 5 um sheets. Surface erosion (delta about one 5 um sheet) at 30 um per year needs D = v*delta = 5e-18 m2/s and k = v/delta = 2e-7 1/s; a water diffusivity of 5e-18 m2/s is about 4 orders below polyesters and polyanhydrides (1e-14 to 1e-12). The Peclet number v*T/D = 3e-3 confirms that surface recession does not shape the profile. The concept therefore fails as parameterised; a working variant would need a different trigger (hydrolysable interlayers that are reached only at the surface, or a leached-layer mechanism as in self-polishing copolymers, whose polishing rates are 5-15 um per month and would consume 0.3 mm in 2-5 years). Separately, the drag benefit is indirect and the model cannot compute it, and biocide-free surface renewal is too slow to stop barnacle cyprids that cement within hours. The request itself remains feasible.
